author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Raynham police arrested a 17-year-old Friday morning after authorities were alerted to alleged school-shooting and bomb threats posted on an online gaming platform, NBC 10 reported. The teenager's name was not released because the case is in juvenile court.

Police Chief David LaPlante said the FBI notified local investigators after the platform flagged the messages. Officers identified the teenager, searched for weapons and assessed whether there was an immediate danger. Police said the threat was not credible, the teen did not have access to weapons and no weapons were found. Officers nevertheless increased their presence at local schools as a precaution.

The teenager was expected to be arraigned in juvenile court. The allegations have not been proven, and the case remains subject to the protections and procedures of the juvenile justice system. Officials urged families to report concerning online statements rather than attempting to investigate them independently. The incident also highlights the increasingly important role that gaming and social platforms play in detecting threats and quickly forwarding information to law enforcement for assessment.
dek: Police said an FBI alert led to the arrest of a 17-year-old and that investigators found no weapons or evidence of a credible plan.
headline: Raynham teen arrested after online school threat, police say
